---
title: Ollama Embeddings
guide-section: Building a Store
---

[Ollama](https://ollama.com) runs chat and embedding models on your computer. You download a model with `ollama pull`, then use Ollama's API to create embeddings. With a local model, the text you embed stays on your machine, and you don't need an API key.

raghilda connects to this API through `EmbeddingOllama`. This guide shows how to set it up, choose a model, and connect to an Ollama server on your computer or another machine.

## Installation

First, download and install Ollama from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com/download). Once it's running, pull an embedding model from the command line:

```bash
ollama pull embeddinggemma-2
```

This guide uses Google's [EmbeddingGemma 2](https://ollama.com/library/embeddinggemma-2), raghilda's default Ollama model. The download is about 1.3 GB, and the model supports an 8,192-token context window.

You don't need any additional Python packages. `EmbeddingOllama` uses the `openai` client library, which already comes with raghilda.

## Basic usage

Once Ollama is running and you've downloaded the model, create a provider with EmbeddingGemma's query and document prompts. By default, it connects to `http://localhost:11434/v1` and uses `embeddinggemma-2:latest`:

```{python}
#| eval: false
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingOllama, EmbedInputType

provider = EmbeddingOllama(
    prompts={
        EmbedInputType.QUERY: "task: search result | query: ",
        EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT: "title: none | text: ",
    },
)
```

These prefixes tell the model whether it is embedding a search query or a document. The provider adds them to the text sent to Ollama; your stored text stays unchanged. See [task-specific prompts](#task-specific-prompts) for details.

Pass the provider to a store through the `embed=` argument:

```{python}
#| eval: false
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="my_store.db",
    embed=provider,
)
```

Creating a store makes a request to Ollama to determine the embedding size. Ollama needs to be running and the model needs to be downloaded before you call `create()`.

## Choosing a model

EmbeddingGemma 2 is the suggested starting point for this guide. It is available from Google's release through Ollama's official model library. Its download size and context window make it a practical option for local document search. If you only need text embeddings, the 270M version leaves out the image and audio encoders for a smaller download.

These examples were reviewed in November 2026:

| Ollama model                                                                | Dimensions | Notes                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`embeddinggemma-2:latest`](https://ollama.com/library/embeddinggemma-2)    | 768        | raghilda's default; used in this guide                   |
| [`embeddinggemma-2:270m`](https://ollama.com/library/embeddinggemma-2:270m) | 768        | Text-only version; omits the image and audio encoders    |
| [`qwen3-embedding:0.6b`](https://ollama.com/library/qwen3-embedding:0.6b)   | 1024       | Alternative for text retrieval; uses a query instruction |

To use a different model, download it first, then pass its name exactly as it appears in `ollama list` to `model=`. For example, run `ollama pull embeddinggemma-2:270m`, then add `model="embeddinggemma-2:270m"` to the provider above. Both EmbeddingGemma 2 variants use the same prompts. Other models may need different prompts; check the publisher's model card before switching.

When comparing models, consider the publisher, how widely the model is used, download size, and context length alongside retrieval benchmarks. Try questions with known answers and check whether the retrieved passages contain those answers. Record response time and memory use on the machine where you plan to run it.

Browse [Ollama's model search page](https://ollama.com/search?c=embedding) for other options. To see which models you've already downloaded, run `ollama list`.

::: {.callout-note}
Use the same model and prompt configuration throughout a store. To switch models or change document prefixes, create a new store and embed your documents again.
:::

## Task-specific prompts

Omitting a model's recommended prefixes can reduce retrieval quality without raising an error. Set `prompts=` when creating the provider, as in the example above. The keys are `EmbedInputType.QUERY` and `EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT`; each value is the prefix to add for that kind of text. With no prompts configured, the provider sends text unchanged.

The store selects the input type for you: `upsert()` and `ingest()` use `DOCUMENT`, while `retrieve()` uses `QUERY`. When calling `embed()` directly, pass the query type explicitly:

```{python}
#| eval: false
query_embeddings = provider.embed(
    ["How do I configure authentication?"],
    input_type=EmbedInputType.QUERY,
)
```

The default input type is `DOCUMENT`. EmbeddingGemma's [model card](https://huggingface.co/google/embeddinggemma-2#1-task-instruction-prefixes) lists its prompts for search, code retrieval, and other tasks. The document prefix in this guide uses `title: none` because the provider receives text without a separate title field.

## Connecting to Ollama on another machine

If Ollama runs on a different machine or port, set `base_url=` to its address:

```{python}
#| eval: false
provider = EmbeddingOllama(
    base_url="http://192.168.1.10:11434/v1",
    prompts={
        EmbedInputType.QUERY: "task: search result | query: ",
        EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT: "title: none | text: ",
    },
)
```

Include `/v1` in the URL to use Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API. By default, Ollama only accepts connections from the machine it's running on. To accept connections from other machines, configure `OLLAMA_HOST` on the server as described in [Ollama's FAQ](https://docs.ollama.com/faq).

The local Ollama server doesn't require an API key. If your server is behind a proxy that requires one, supply it with `api_key=`.

## Reconnecting to a store

`DuckDBStore.connect()` restores the provider's saved model name, server address, batch size, and prompts:

```{python}
#| eval: false
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore

store = DuckDBStore.connect("my_store.db")
```

Ollama needs to be running at the saved address, with the model available, when you add documents or search the store. A local Ollama server doesn't require an API key when reconnecting either.

::: {.callout-tip}
Use `EmbeddingOllama` when creating a store with Ollama. A store created with `EmbeddingOpenAI(base_url=...)` restores an OpenAI provider when you reconnect, which requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` to be set.
:::

## Troubleshooting

**Connection errors.** If you see an `APIConnectionError` (or a "connection refused" message), raghilda couldn't reach Ollama at the configured `base_url`. Check that the Ollama app is running, or start the server yourself with `ollama serve`. If Ollama is on another machine, double-check the address and port.

**Model not found.** An error like `model 'embeddinggemma-2:latest' not found` means Ollama is running but the model hasn't been pulled. Run `ollama pull embeddinggemma-2` (or whichever model you've configured) and try again.

For other errors, Ollama's [troubleshooting guide](https://docs.ollama.com/troubleshooting) explains where to find the server logs.

## Parameters

`EmbeddingOllama` accepts these optional parameters:

| Parameter    | Default                       | Description                                                                 |
| ------------ | ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`      | `"embeddinggemma-2:latest"`   | Ollama embedding model name, as shown by `ollama list`                      |
| `base_url`   | `"http://localhost:11434/v1"` | Address of Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API                                   |
| `api_key`    | `None`                        | Only needed behind an authenticating proxy. A placeholder is used if `None` |
| `batch_size` | `20`                          | Texts per API call                                                          |
| `prompts`    | `None`                        | Optional prefix strings keyed by `EmbedInputType`                           |

The store saves `model`, `base_url`, `batch_size`, and any `prompts`. It doesn't save `api_key`. See the [`EmbeddingOllama` reference page](/reference/embedding.EmbeddingOllama.qmd) for API details.

## Complete example

This example builds a store from two web pages and searches it, using Ollama to embed the text locally. Replace the example URLs with pages you want to search:

```{python}
#| eval: false
from raghilda.store import DuckDBStore
from raghilda.embedding import EmbeddingOllama, EmbedInputType
from raghilda.read import read_as_markdown
from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker

store = DuckDBStore.create(
    location="docs.db",
    embed=EmbeddingOllama(
        prompts={
            EmbedInputType.QUERY: "task: search result | query: ",
            EmbedInputType.DOCUMENT: "title: none | text: ",
        },
    ),
    name="docs",
    title="My Documentation",
    overwrite=True,
)

chunker = MarkdownChunker()
for url in ["https://example.com/doc1", "https://example.com/doc2"]:
    store.upsert(chunker.chunk(read_as_markdown(url)))

store.build_index()

chunks = store.retrieve("How do I configure authentication?", top_k=5)
for chunk in chunks:
    print(chunk.text[:200])
```

You can also use `ChatOllama` in [chatlas](chatlas-integration.qmd) to run the chat model locally.

## Using Ollama with ChromaDB

When you pass `EmbeddingOllama` to `ChromaDBStore`, raghilda wraps it in an adapter so that ChromaDB can call it. The provider applies the configured query and document prefixes and is restored automatically when you reconnect from Python. ChromaDB clients in other languages won't be able to use the collection's embedding function. See [ChromaDB Embedding Functions](chromadb-embedding-functions.qmd) for details.

## Other local embedding options

[SentenceTransformers](embedding-sentence-transformers.qmd) also supports local embeddings. It loads the model inside your Python process. Ollama runs models in a separate server, which can accept requests from several applications.
